faq.q: What is the difference between live resin and live rosin?
faq.a: Both start with flower frozen at harvest. Live resin is extracted with a solvent like butane, then purged; live rosin uses only ice water, heat and pressure. Rosin costs more and is sold by brands like A1 Ducksauce; MFNY and Olio are the main live resin makers in New York.

faq.q: How much concentrate can I buy?
faq.a: New York's possession limit for concentrate is 24 grams, separate from the three-ounce flower limit. Dispensaries sell single grams and occasionally half-grams, so the limit rarely matters in practice.

faq.a: Gummies and chocolate typically take 30 minutes to two hours, since THC is absorbed through digestion. Drinks from brands like Layup and Ayrloom use water-soluble THC and many people feel them in 15 to 30 minutes. Start with 5 milligrams or less if you are new.

faq.a: A small 0.7-gram bag of flower, sold by 5 Boro and a few other brands. It is enough for one or two joints and the cheapest way to try a strain before committing to an eighth.

faq.q: How do I use a cannabis tincture?
faq.a: Measure a dose with the dropper, hold it under your tongue for 30 to 60 seconds, then swallow. Onset is usually 15 to 45 minutes, faster than an edible, and the bottle label gives milligrams per dropper so you can start small.

faq.q: What is the difference between a cartridge and an all-in-one?
faq.a: A cartridge screws onto a separate rechargeable 510-thread battery and can be swapped out. An all-in-one, or disposable, has the battery built in and is discarded when empty. Pod systems like PAX and Plug Play use proprietary pods with their own battery.
